external_entities.name: Member
external_entities.description: A library member who uses the library app and self-service kiosks to borrow, renew, reserve, and return books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
external_entities.notes: The member's authentication mechanism is not stated.

external_entities.name: Desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk personnel who manually extend loans, clear account blocks, and mark books returned.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: All desk staff use the same shared circulation-page login; individual identity and branch are not recorded.

processes.name: Library app
processes.description: The app on a member's phone that requests loan renewals and reservations from the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.
processes.notes: The app's authentication mechanism is uncertain: Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."

processes.name: Self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where members scan their library card and books, sending loans and returns to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
processes.notes: The kiosk's technology and authentication are not stated.

processes.name: Lending API
processes.description: The REST service that is the sole stated reader and writer of the loans database and handles member loan and reservation operations.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: The written note says, "The lending API is internal-only." The interview says, "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet." These are conflicting exposure claims. Authentication behavior for phone calls is uncertain: Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."

data_stores.name: Loans database
data_stores.description: The single database containing members, names, email addresses, home addresses, borrowing history, loans, and reservations.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: Priya corrected the earlier description of two databases: "We merged those in the spring. It's one loans database now. The old reservations database is gone."

data_flows.name: borrow books
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to initiate borrowing, renewal, or reservation activity.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
data_flows.notes: The app's authentication mechanism is not stated.
data_flows.data_description: Member and book or title activity for borrowing, renewal, or reservation.

data_flows.name: renew or reserve
data_flows.description: The library app sends a renewal or reservation request to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.notes: Authentication is uncertain: Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."
data_flows.data_description: The member and book for a renewal, or the member and title for a reservation.

data_flows.name: send loans
data_flows.description: A self-service kiosk sends each scanned loan and return to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API.
data_flows.notes: What the kiosks communicate with besides the lending API is not known.
data_flows.data_description: Scanned member, book, loan, and return information.

data_flows.name: update account
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page served by the lending API to extend loans, clear blocks, or mark books returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.
data_flows.notes: The circulation page uses one shared login. The password is on a card taped under the desk, and the history records only that the loan was closed by hand.
data_flows.data_description: Loan extensions, account-block changes, and manual book-return records.

data_flows.name: store loan changes
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations, borrowing history, and account-related changes.

trust_boundaries.name: Branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which the self-service kiosks and desk staff operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: Council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data-centre zone where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database is confidential because it contains members' names, email addresses, home addresses, and full borrowing histories.
assumptions.basis: The interview states that these personal details and borrowing histories live in the loans database.
